spec_text_vs_execution_drift.details: AC4 states 'CandidatesSidebar reads from PLAN_DATA.trips[activeTrip].days[activeDay].slots' as the data source, but PLAN_DATA produced by generate_plan_data() has no 'slots' field. The actual v2 slot/options data is in data/<trip>/days/day-NN.json files, accessible via GET /api/trip/<id> (hydrate_trip returns days[] which are raw day-NN.json content including slots). The BA Tech Hints also reference 'PLAN_DATA.trips[activeTrip].days[activeDay].slots (or equivalent path in the v2 schema)' with a qualifier 'Dev must verify the exact JSON path'. This qualifier signals the BA was uncertain. The path is wrong — dev following this will produce a sidebar with no candidates.
spec_text_vs_execution_drift.proposed_fix: Revise CandidatesSidebar data source in spec and Tech Hints: 'CandidatesSidebar reads from EDITOR_DATA.days[activeDay].slots, where EDITOR_DATA is loaded via fetch("/api/trip/<trip_id>") in a useEffect. The /api/trip/<id> response includes days[] from v2 day-NN.json files with slots[slotId].options[]. Match activeDay to EDITOR_DATA.days by day.day field (integer 1-indexed), not by array index, because selDay in React is grouped-trip-relative while day.day is absolute.'

findings.title: CandidatesSidebar data source path does not exist in PLAN_DATA
findings.location: ticket-20260517-211850.md — AC4, Technical Hints (CandidatesSidebar data source paragraph)
findings.evidence: QA verified: generate_plan_data() produces day.meals.breakfast, day.meals.lunch, day.meals.dinner, day.meal_alternatives, day.attractions etc. — no 'slots' key. Confirmed via Python: python3 -c 'import json,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path("data/beijing-lijiang-dali-20260418-100846/days/day-02.json"); d=json.loads(p.read_text()); print(list(d.keys()))' → ['schema_version', 'day', 'date', 'city_id', 'city_name', 'leg_index', 'day_type', 'stage', 'arrival_ts', 'departure_ts', 'slots', 'accommodation', 'intra_city_routes', 'warnings']. The 'slots' key exists in v2 day-NN.json, NOT in PLAN_DATA.
findings.impact: Dev will attempt to read PLAN_DATA.trips[x].days[y].slots and get undefined. CandidatesSidebar will have no candidates. AC4 will fail — 'candidates-groups contains at least one .card-candidate element' will be false. AC5 (drag-and-drop) and AC6 (day selector updates sidebar) are also untestable.
findings.proposed_fix: CandidatesSidebar must fetch editor data separately: useEffect calls fetch('/api/trip/<trip_id>') and stores EDITOR_DATA.days[] in React state. The candidates for the active day are EDITOR_DATA.days.find(d => d.day === activePublishedDay.day).slots[slotId].options[]. The trip_id must be embedded in the generated HTML (e.g., const TRIP_ID = '__TRIP_ID__'; injected by render_html_builders.py alongside PLAN_DATA).

findings.title: v2 option fields are incompatible with React card rendering — adapter required
findings.location: ticket-20260517-211850.md — M2, M3, M5; Technical Hints (CandidatesSidebar data source)
findings.evidence: QA verified v2 option fields (from day-05.json evening_activity options[0]): {option_id, name, name_local, location_summary, cost (local currency float), currency_local, fit_score, why_fits_user, source_agent, ...}. React KanbanView card expects: name_base, location_base, display-currency cost, notes_base, links (for LinkChip), stars, etc. There is NO name_base, NO location_base in v2 options. Cost is in local CNY, not display EUR. The spec says 'each .card-candidate has data-option-id and data-slot-id' but says nothing about field mapping.
findings.impact: CandidatesSidebar cards will render with blank names and incorrect cost display if dev naively maps v2 option fields to React card props. AC4 and AC5 depend on well-formed candidate cards with correct data.
findings.proposed_fix: Spec must define an adapter: toDisplayCard(option, slotId) => { name_base: option.name, name_local: option.name_local, location_base: option.location_summary, cost: toDisplayCurrency(option.cost, option.currency_local, exchangeRates), option_id: option.option_id, slot_id: slotId }. The exchange rate for the adapter should come from a constant in the generated HTML (CURRENCY_SYMBOL is already injected by render_html_builders.py; extend to include exchange rates as EDITOR_EXCHANGE_RATES).

findings.title: Cache stale-write race: invalidation during generation allows stale HTML to overwrite fresh cache
findings.location: ticket-20260517-211850.md — Finding 1 resolution, Technical Hints (Cache structure)
findings.evidence: The proposed cache pattern is: check lock → miss → generate OUTSIDE lock → write with lock. Two bugs: (1) Two concurrent cold requests both generate and both write — the second write wastes work but is harmless. (2) A /api/save call can invalidate the cache WHILE a generation is running outside the lock. When generation finishes and writes to cache (inside lock), the stale pre-save HTML overwrites the now-empty cache, and subsequent requests see outdated data until the next invalidation. This is a real correctness bug for an editor — user saves a change and then sees stale content on next load.
findings.impact: After /api/save, a concurrent in-flight generation can re-populate cache with pre-save HTML. The user sees their save 'undone' on page reload until the next change triggers another invalidation. AC5 (save triggers correct display) can falsely pass if tested immediately but fail on next page load.
findings.proposed_fix: Use per-trip generation locks: _html_locks: dict[str, threading.Lock] = {}. Take the per-trip lock before generation, hold it through cache write. On invalidation also take the per-trip lock. This prevents the race without blocking ALL trips behind one lock. Alternatively, use a version counter: increment _html_version[trip_id] on save, stamp it during generation, only write to cache if the current version matches the stamped version when writing.

findings.title: CandidatesSidebar in normal flex layout will compress main content area below 960px
findings.evidence: react_template.tpl:1714 wraps main content in: <div style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>. KanbanView caps at max-width: 960px (react_template.tpl:723). At 1440px viewport, Sidebar (left, ~220px) + main (flex:1) = ~1220px for main. Adding CandidatesSidebar (280px fixed) compresses main to ~940px, which is under the 960px max-width cap — the max-width cap would become binding and shrink the main content area below 960px. This changes card layout reflow at exactly the viewport width (1440px) the user uses for comparison.
findings.impact: AC3 (kanban cards are 280px wide) and AC1 visual parity tests at 1440x900 may fail if the main content area is narrower than expected. The user's complaint is 'one-to-one identical' — any layout compression is a failure.
findings.proposed_fix: CandidatesSidebar should be rendered as a fixed-position overlay panel (right: 0, position: fixed, width: 280px) rather than inside the flex layout. Main content reflow is then unaffected. Alternatively, clarify in the spec that parity screenshots are taken with the sidebar hidden/collapsed and that the sidebar is additive outside the main content bounds.

findings.title: window.setEditorSelection bridge pseudocode omits required /api/save payload format
findings.evidence: The spec shows: fetch('/api/save', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({...}) }). The '...' is undefined. The actual /api/save endpoint (web/js/save.js or server handler) expects a specific mutation format. React's selDay is zero-based within a grouped trip (PLAN_DATA.trips[selTrip].days[selDay]) but the API day field is absolute (day.day integer from day-NN.json). Mapping selDay to the absolute day.day requires: PLAN_DATA.trips[selTrip].days[selDay].day.
findings.impact: Dev will likely pass the wrong day index to /api/save, causing mutations to land on the wrong day. AC5 depends on /api/save firing correctly.
findings.proposed_fix: Spec must show the complete save payload: { trip_id: TRIP_ID, day: activeDay.day, editor_session: Date.now().toString(), mutations: [{ type: 'select', slot: slotId, option_id: optionId, origin_slot_id: originSlotId || null }] }. Verify against the actual /api/save handler in serve-trip.py or the existing web/js/save.js reference implementation.

findings.title: Option A category-to-slot mapping is undefined and likely wrong
findings.location: ticket-20260517-211850.md — Finding 4 (drop zones), Technical Hints (Option A drop zone placement)
findings.evidence: Spec: 'meals section → breakfast (primary meal slot), attractions → morning_activity, etc.' But v2 slots are: breakfast, morning_activity, lunch, afternoon_activity, dinner, evening_activity. The meals KanbanView section header contains all three meal cards (breakfast/lunch/dinner) — mapping the entire meals section to just 'breakfast' loses lunch and dinner drop targets. The attractions section similarly may map to morning_activity or afternoon_activity depending on timeline. The 'etc.' is unspecified.
findings.impact: Dev will produce drop zones that only cover breakfast and morning_activity, missing lunch, dinner, and afternoon/evening slots. Users cannot drag candidates for non-breakfast meals.
findings.proposed_fix: Either: (a) Specify the full slot-to-category header mapping in the spec (e.g., add drop zones per-card in KanbanView, one per displayed meal card, using the card's actual slot key), or (b) Recommend switching to slot-granular drop zones rather than category-header drop zones (one .slot-drop per card, with data-slot-id matching the card's slot key).

root_cause_verification.rationale: QA confirmed from source: web/css/main.css:6 imports Inter via Google Fonts (@import url(...Inter...)). web/index.html:72 has . web/index.html:39 has 3-panel layout (#pane-days | #pane-middle | #pane-candidates). react_template.tpl:1704 has fontFamily: 'ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, ...' react_template.tpl:726-729 has 200px background-div cover. react_template.tpl:784-785 has cardW=280, cardH=320. finding_1_exchange_rate.details: The subprocess does run during InteractiveHTMLGenerator.__init__() (lines 48, 52-75 of generate-html-interactive.py) with timeout=10. The cache approach is correct. But the cache write pattern has a race condition (see F3 above). Additionally, the spec says AC8 is 'second request < 2s' but does not address that the FIRST request can still block 10s for every trip on cold start. This is declared acceptable for a local dev tool which is reasonable.

finding_2_importlib.details: QA confirmed: generate-html-interactive.py exists at scripts/generate-html-interactive.py (Python cannot import hyphenated names). scripts/lib/html_generator.py exists and contains TravelPlanHTMLGenerator (different class — NOT InteractiveHTMLGenerator). So dev must use importlib pattern. The importlib code in Technical Hints is syntactically correct.

finding_3_statejs_autoinit.details: QA confirmed: web/js/state.js line 879-881 calls init() on DOMContentLoaded or immediately if DOM is ready. init() (line 118) calls document.getElementById on trip-title (line 180), approve-day-btn (line 591), tab-timeline (line 831), candidates-groups (line 283) — none of which exist in the React-rendered DOM. state.js must not be injected. Confirmed.

finding_4_drop_zones.details: Correct that KanbanView has no .slot-drop elements. Option A vs Option B assessment is reasonable. However the category-to-slot mapping in Option A is underspecified and likely wrong (see F6). Option B (TimelineView) is less suitable because it departs from the Notion Kanban visual parity the user demands.

finding_5_react_bridge.details: window.setEditorSelection inside useEffect is the correct pattern for bridging vanilla JS events into React state. But save payload format is missing (see F5). Also: the bridge must clean up on component unmount (return a cleanup function from useEffect that sets window.setEditorSelection = null or a no-op).

finding_6_editor_mode.details: HTML_SCRIPT is a constant string at render_html_builders.py:344-354. String replacement to inject EDITOR_MODE is straightforward. However: the published generate_html() function must also emit EDITOR_MODE=false (not omit it), otherwise published pages that add an EDITOR_MODE check to the JSX will crash with ReferenceError. This is confirmed by Codex finding #12.

option_a_vs_option_b_assessment.recommendation: Option A (KanbanView drop zones) is architecturally more sound for the stated requirement because it preserves the Notion Kanban visual context during editing. However, Option A's recommended per-category-header placement is wrong — it should be per-slot-card overlays, not per-section-header overlays. The spec should clarify: one invisible .slot-drop overlay per card, using the card's actual slot_id (breakfast/lunch/dinner/morning_activity etc.), rendered as position:absolute overlays (not adding height) only when EDITOR_MODE=true and during drag-active state. This preserves visual parity while providing slot-precise drop targets.

r2_feature_completeness_check.finding: R2 acceptance criterion states: 'Editor retains all published-page features (language toggle, map provider toggle, timeline view, budget, item detail sidebar) PLUS adds candidates sidebar and drag-and-drop'. The spec correctly marks web/js/mobile.js, web/js/save.js, web/js/routing.js, web/js/budget.js, web/js/offline.js as out-of-path. However, the spec does not explicitly state how their equivalent functionality is preserved in the React editor. The React template already has language toggle (setLang), map provider toggle (setMapProvider), timeline view (setView), budget (Donut component), and item detail sidebar (selectedItem state). These are preserved by construction through sharing the React template. The spec should explicitly call this out to prevent dev from accidentally removing these features.
r2_feature_completeness_check.verdict: acceptable — preserved by construction; minor documentation gap only

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex confirmed all 3 critical findings independently. Key Codex findings: (1) React template approach is architecturally correct (PROPOSED_FIX: share react_template.tpl as single rendering template). (2) BA's PLAN_DATA.trips[...].days[...].slots path is wrong — correct source is GET /api/trip/<id> v2 days[n].slots. (3) Static PLAN_DATA and editor save state are different data models — PLAN_DATA is from legacy meals.json/attractions.json, save writes to v2 day-NN.json. (4) v2 options are not directly render-compatible with React cards — need adapter. (5) CandidatesSidebar in flex layout can compress main content area below 960px. (6) Option A category mapping is flawed (meals section maps to breakfast only, missing lunch/dinner). (7) Visible .slot-drop headers threaten visual parity — should be invisible overlays. (8) Cache double-checked locking has stale-write race. (9) First request still blocks 10s (cache only helps second). (10) drag.js module-boundary risk — mobile.js also imports state.js. (11) window.setEditorSelection pseudocode omits save payload format. (12) EDITOR_MODE must be emitted as false in published HTML too. (13) OBSERVATION_ONLY: candidate scarcity in PLAN_DATA is a data issue not architecture issue.
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Codex findings 2, 3, 4 confirmed F1 and F2 in this report. Codex finding 8 confirmed F3. Codex findings 5, 6, 7 supported F4. Codex finding 11 confirmed F5. Codex finding 6 confirmed F6. Codex finding 12 added to Technical Findings assessment (Finding 6). Codex findings 9, 10 added as additional context in respective assessments. Codex finding 13 (OBSERVATION_ONLY) noted: acknowledged but classified as non-blocking since v2 day-NN.json does have multi-option slots (day-05 evening_activity has 4 options), confirming v2 is viable once the correct path is specified.
